words.gloss: than those who have not learned

literal: Than those who have not learned, the lowest, they say, [are those who] having learned and known, fear the assembly of the good.
translation: They say that those who fear to face an assembly of the wise, even though they have studied and acquired knowledge, are worse than the unlearned.
modern: கற்றுக்கொண்டு எல்லாவற்றையும் அறிந்திருந்தாலும், நல்லவர்களுடைய அவைக்கு அஞ்சுபவர்களை, கல்லாதவர்களை விடக் கடைசியானவர்கள் என்று கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of education without the courage to speak before an audience. The author states that people who have studied deeply and acquired vast knowledge, yet tremble with fear when facing an assembly of wise and good people, are considered inferior even to those who are completely uneducated. The key words 'கற்று அறிந்தும்' (even though having learned and known) contrast sharply with 'கல்லாதவரின் கடை' (lower than the unlearned), emphasizing that knowledge is useless if it cannot be expressed confidently in public. The term 'நல்லார் அவை' refers to an assembly of noble or learned people, which is the ultimate testing ground for one's learning.
